chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from al-Abbas ibn Amir and Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, both from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about one who departs from his home with falcons and dogs, staying away for two or three nights, whether he shortens his prayer or not. He said: 'He does not shorten [his prayer], for he has gone out for amusement.'

key_terms.يَتَنَزَّهُ: to stay away / to go for a sojourn

ai.seo_question: Does a traveler shorten their prayer if they are traveling for leisure or hunting?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Zura'ah asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) whether a traveler engaging in leisure activities like falconry and hunting for two or three nights is entitled to shorten prayers. The Imam clarifies that such a person does not shorten their prayer because their journey is classified as 'lahw' (amusement/entertainment) rather than a purposeful journey for necessity or work, highlighting the Shia juristic distinction between the intent and nature of travel in determining legal concessions.
